A desk tracker deck for M8 Headless

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

14SPOR-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    GNDKeypad controller G · Edit key 2 · Option key 2 · Play key 2 · Shift key 2 · Right key 2 · Left key 2 · Down key 2 · Up key 2
    KEY_EDITKeypad controller 18 · Edit key 1
    KEY_OPTIONKeypad controller 17 · Option key 1
    KEY_PLAYKeypad controller 16 · Play key 1
    KEY_SHIFTKeypad controller 15 · Shift key 1
    KEY_RIGHTKeypad controller 7 · Right key 1
    KEY_LEFTKeypad controller 6 · Left key 1
    KEY_DOWNKeypad controller 5 · Down key 1
    KEY_UPKeypad controller 4 · Up key 1
  3. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  4. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
15SPOR-WIRE-1

Spor is built

Spor puts a Teensy 4.1 running Dirtywave's M8 Headless firmware and an eight-key keypad in one printed case. Plug both USB cables into a laptop, open m8c, and you play the tracker with real keys instead of a computer keyboard, with audio coming back over USB. The Teensy runs the official precompiled firmware untouched; the keypad is a small ESP32-S3 that types the keys m8c expects.
